sections.h2: Where does Roxboro file its deeds?
sections.html:
The courthouse-area office is 21 Abbitt Street in Roxboro (ZIP 27573). Its listed number is (336) 597-1733. The Tax Office, which you will also need, is at 13 Abbitt.

County materials describe the department as the custodian of Person County's most important records. Visitors come for:

  • searches of land records
  • vital records, meaning births, deaths and marriages
  • marriage licenses and notary oaths
  • plats, cemetery records, grave removals, military discharges and genealogy files

Sellers mostly want the first item and the filing of the deed. Phone before you go to learn counter hours and whether electronic filing is offered.

sections.h2: How many properties does the Person County deed office serve?
sections.html:
Roughly 19,000 homes and apartments (19,023 housing units, per QuickFacts for July 2025) fall under this office, on 392.34 square miles of land. Of the homes lived in during 2020 to 2024, 77.3% were occupied by their owners, and those owner homes had a median value of $213,900.

The county counted 16,063 households and about 40,636 people, a 4.0% rise over the 2020 base. Builders pulled just 145 permits in 2025, so most deeds record a resale of an existing house rather than a new build.

  • Owners with a mortgage: $1,393 a month at the median.
  • Median gross rent: $864.
  • Share of residents 65 or older: 23.4%.

On a house in that value range, a flat filing fee and a tax of $1.00 per $500.00 are small pieces of the closing statement. Your title and tax payoff matter far more.

sections.h2: Who is the register, and why does filing order matter?
sections.html:
An elected officer holds the post, with a two-year term (G.S. 161-1). The office takes in conveyances, applies the uniform charges, and collects excise tax before anything goes on record (G.S. 161-10).

Ranking is by time stamp. Under G.S. 47-18, a deed or a lease of more than three years binds neither lien creditors nor purchasers for value until it is registered in the land's own county.

Clerks will not draft a deed or settle who owns what. An unfiled deed gives you no protection, which is why your attorney should file it the moment funds are released.

sections.h2: What will recording a Person County deed cost me?
sections.html:
Every figure is fixed by the legislature, so the Roxboro counter has no discretion.

Charges set by G.S. 161-10 and collected at the Person County counter
FilingCharge
Deed or other general instrument, 15 pages$26.00
Page 16 onward, general instruments$4.00 per page
Deed of trust or mortgage, 35 pages$64.00
Release of a deed of trustNo fee
Map or plat$21.00 per sheet
Certified copy$5.00 for page one, $2.00 per page after
Document in nonstandard form$25.00 extra
Additional instrument within one document$10.00 each

Pay before filing. Paying off an old loan ahead of listing costs nothing at this counter.

sections.h2: Who pays the excise stamp tax on a Roxboro deed?
sections.html:
Whoever gives up title pays, which in a sale is the seller. The tax is due before the deed is filed, and G.S. 105-228.30 sets it at $1.00 for each $500.00 or part of it in price or value.

The county retains half. The state receives the remainder monthly, after refunds and an allowance. A tract that spans counties pays where more of its value lies.

  • Put it on your net sheet, since it reduces what you take home.
  • It tracks the price in your contract.
  • If a gift or family transfer has little stated value, ask the office how it handles that.

Get the figure from your attorney in writing ahead of closing day.

sections.h2: What should I look for in Person County land records before listing?
sections.html:
Take an hour in the index, or pay an attorney to, and hunt for anything that blocks a clean transfer. Old unreleased loans, judgments and forgotten options are the usual finds.

  • Seller names should match the last recorded deed.
  • The contract's legal description should match that deed's.
  • Every earlier deed of trust needs a recorded release.
  • Ask the Tax Office for the balance so the lien clears at closing.

If you financed a buyer yourself, Chapter 47H has you record the contract or a brief memorandum within five business days.

One call to the old lender usually fixes a missing release. Title held by a deceased owner is a bigger job. A cash buyer can move fast, though insurable title still comes first.

sections.h2: How should I prepare a deed for filing?
sections.html:
Bring the signed, notarized original with the tax payment and fee, and check the page count, since each extra page adds four dollars.

Order of events counts. The buyer's lender normally files its deed of trust right after the deed, and your own payoff releases should already be in motion.

  • Look over the notary block for a full date and signature.
  • Add the parcel number to page one if your attorney does.
  • Keep a copy with the registration time on it.

Ask whether the office takes electronic filing, and confirm counter hours before driving over.

sections.h2: Can I order a certified copy of an old deed or a plat?
sections.html:
Yes, the office searches and copies land records, and the statewide schedule sets the price for certified copies and for filing a plat. Ask the staff whether a copy can be requested by mail or phone, since this page does not list that.

An older deed is useful for three reasons when you plan a sale:

  • It shows the exact words used for the boundary, which a buyer's surveyor will compare against the ground.
  • It names the people who held title before you, which confirms the chain.
  • It may refer to an easement, a road right, or a restriction that survives to the new owner.

Copies are priced per page (see the table), and a plat is filed per sheet. If you ordered a new survey as part of dividing land, the plat is recorded here before lots are sold separately.

Bring the tax parcel number and the names of recent owners to speed up the search, and ask staff which index years cover the period you need. Staff cannot interpret what a deed means, so take any unclear wording to an attorney or surveyor.

sections.h2: What do I do if the owner of record has died?
sections.html:
A deed signed by someone who has died cannot be treated as a normal conveyance, so an estate attorney should say who may sign for the owner. State law lets small estates collect personal property by affidavit, with a cap of $20,000 in G.S. 28A-25-1, and that affidavit lists each tract of land the person owned.

  • Gather a death certificate, which the deed office keeps among its vital records.
  • Search the land records for the last recorded deed to confirm what the person actually owned.
  • Speak with an estate attorney before anyone signs a deed.

An heir who wants a quick sale should know that title company and lender requirements usually decide the timeline, not the filing counter.

faqs.a: 21 Abbitt Street, Roxboro, NC 27573. The county directory lists (336) 597-1733, and the office can give you counter hours.

faqs.q: What does a deed filing run?
faqs.a: The statute prices a deed at $26.00 through page 15, then $4.00 a page. See the table above for loans, plats and copies.

faqs.q: Who pays the stamp tax when a home sells?
faqs.a: The seller does, to the register, before filing. The statute's rate is $1.00 per $500.00 or part of the value.

faqs.q: Do I pay to record the release of my old mortgage?
faqs.a: No. The fee schedule lists no charge for releases of deeds of trust or mortgages.

faqs.q: Why does the filing time matter?
faqs.a: Priority follows the time of registration, and an unfiled conveyance loses to lien creditors and paying buyers.
